A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeNVeR and the XACV dataset. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original XACV segmentation results and component ablations in Tables 1–2, CADICA qualitative comparisons, and additional segmentation and temporal-coherency results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original segmentation experiments and reports additional supervised comparisons, ROC/PR results, prior-quality experiments, and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The reported mask-consistency objective changes: v1 Equation 9 compares consecutive masks at identical coordinates, whereas v2 Equation 5 compares against flow-warped next-frame masks. The two-stage architecture and other substantive loss definitions remain. Newly specified Otsu thresholding and architecture details do not establish additional procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate coronary X-ray video segmentation using XACV and qualitative CADICA comparisons. XCAD remains a dataset illustration rather than an added evaluation benchmark. The newly disclosed patient count, frame statistics, and acquisition details describe the existing 111-video XACV collection.

E2.justification: v2 adds supervised U-Net to the quantitative XACV comparison in Table 1 and to the main XACV and CADICA visual comparisons. v1 already includes image/video supervised comparisons in its appendix, so supervised evaluation is not entirely new. Hessian, SSVS, DARL, and FreeCOS remain; the newly discussed SVS-Net is not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds AUROC/AUPRC evaluation using final-layer outputs normalized to [0,1], alongside protocols for prior replacement and loss-weight sweeps. The 8:2 split and at least 100 epochs for self-supervised baselines remain. Appendix A.4 reports lambda_smooth=0.001, conflicting with 0.02 retained in Section 4.3, so the actual setting change is unresolved.

E4.justification: The diagnostic evidence expands substantially beyond the original component removals and temporal-coherency visualization. New Appendix A.3 tests dependence on prior quality by substituting FreeCOS predictions; A.5 tests sensitivity to four loss-related weights. The existing component-ablation results are also revised, while the original temporal analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same value-plus-minus-spread reporting format, including for the added supervised row. Neither version specifies repeated-run or seed counts or explains the spread, and v2 adds no confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 2 Dice scores without bootstrapping, prior loss, and parallel loss change from 0.7284/0.7276/0.7292 to 0.6462/0.6333/0.6971; the full-model 0.7339 and shared Table 1 scores remain unchanged. Added results include U-Net Dice 0.771, DeNVeR/FreeCOS AUROC tied at 0.83 and AUPRC 0.78/0.73, and a reported 2.5% Dice improvement using FreeCOS priors. Figure 14 additionally shows substantial F1 deterioration at large reconstruction-loss weights.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 adds an explicit assumption that vessel topology remains unchanged over the approximately three-second clip and revises the mathematical mask-consistency definition to incorporate motion compensation. Other loss equations are substantively retained despite regrouping and renumbering; neither version presents theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain unsupervised test-time vessel segmentation, optical-flow and layer-based temporal modeling, and the first annotated XACV video dataset. The contribution bullets and conclusion retain their substantive claims. The expanded abstract mainly brings forward components and generalization claims already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 expands interpretation of supervised in-domain performance versus CADICA domain gaps and the tradeoff between computation and annotation effort. It extends the original preprocessing-error limitation with runtime/resource constraints and inapplicability without contrast-agent flow. Appendix A.5 adds a broad robustness interpretation, although Figure 14 shows considerable reconstruction-weight sensitivity.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands documentation: Otsu thresholding, shared baseline postprocessing and Dice-based threshold selection, latent-code initialization, MLP dimensions, U-Net depth and convolution settings, and batch size 16. It also details XACV patients, acquisition, annotation, and data handling and promises future public release. These are largely disclosures, not established implementation changes; the conflicting smoothness weights limit reproducibility.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Hao et al. on sequential vessel segmentation, Holynski et al. on Eulerian motion, Otsu, and the AUROC/AUPRC references by Bradley and Boyd et al. It expands positioning against supervised sequential methods and more explicitly credits Eulerian-motion research. Most related work is retained.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, condenses the method overview and several captions, and expands explanatory passages while retaining the main section sequence and much original prose. Appendix A.3–A.5 add clearly named subsections. Citation style changes from numbered to author-date.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 2 with clearer motion components and training annotations, expands Table 1 and the main comparison montages with U-Net, and adds ROC/PR, prior-quality, and hyperparameter plots. The document template and figure placement also change. Original appendix segmentation and temporal panels are retained and renumbered rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the supervised performance gap explicit in Table 1 and supplies architecture details missing from v1. Added diagnostics and practical limitations improve assessability. These benefits are tempered by unexplained large ablation-score revisions, conflicting smoothness weights in Section 4.3 and Appendix A.4, and a blanket robustness claim contradicted by Figure 14. The net improvement is useful but limited.
